threads.thread_goal: Align on project scope, roles, and initial mapping of current shelves

messages.text: Kicking off the Clinic Retail Corner and Supply Shelf Optimisation project. Goal is to standardise layout and processes so shelves are safer, easier to work with, and clearer for patients. For this first step we need to map what we have today for T1 and agree which shelves and zones are in scope for the layout map in A1. From my walk-through this morning I see at least: front retail corner (OTC meds, supplements, small food items), reception counter display, treatment room consumables shelves, clean utility cupboard, and the small fridge in the treatment room. Can you add anything I missed and flag current pain points when you are trying to find or restock items?

Adding a couple more spots I work on a lot: the overstock shelves in the back room where we keep extra bandages and gloves, and the small stand next to the waiting area chairs with leaflets and a few retail items. Pain points I see: similar cough syrups split across two shelves, and some vitamins mixed with dressings on the same shelf. Also the back room overstock is not labelled clearly so I have to open boxes to check what is inside.

From the clinical side, I would definitely include: sharps and blood collection supplies drawer in the treatment room, wound care trolley, and the locked cupboard for high-risk meds. Even if we do not move the locked cupboard itself, we should map it in A1 so the zoning is complete. Pain points: dressings with different sizes are scattered, and some sterile packs are stored next to non-sterile items which makes checks slower.

Agree with what has been listed so far. I would also add the small cupboard behind reception where we keep sample packs and some patient education materials. It affects patient flow when we have to step away from the desk to find things. For scope, I suggest we include all areas where patients can see or reach products plus all clinical supply storage that nurses and assistants use daily. That way T1 and A1 cover the full picture before we design anything new.

On the mapping for T1, I can help photograph the current shelves this afternoon: front retail corner, reception counter display, waiting area stand, treatment room shelves, clean utility cupboard, and the fridge. I will also note where we currently mix food items with medical products so we can fix that later for hygiene.

Question on scope: do we also include the locked drug cabinet in the nurse office, or is that handled under a different protocol? I can take photos of the outside but not sure if we should document the inside layout in A1.

For the locked cabinet, we should map the categories and zones but not individual controlled items. So in A1 we can show sections like emergency meds, injectables, and so on, without listing specific products. That keeps us aligned with clinical protocols while still making the zoning clear for T1.

Yes, I agree with that approach. We can include the locked cabinet in scope as a zone, but keep the detailed contents in our clinical records only. I will check with the health and safety officer to confirm they are comfortable with that and update here if they want any extra notes added to A1.

Let me summarise the areas we have so far for scope: 1) Front retail corner (OTC, supplements, small food items). 2) Reception counter display. 3) Waiting area stand. 4) Treatment room consumables shelves and trolley. 5) Clean utility cupboard. 6) Treatment room fridge. 7) Back room overstock shelves. 8) Cupboard behind reception with samples and leaflets. 9) Locked meds cabinet as a high-level zone only. If everyone is ok with this list, we can treat it as the final scope for A1 and T1.
Scope list looks complete to me. I do not see any other shelves that would affect patients or daily clinical work. Happy to work from that for the mapping.
Agree with that scope as well. It covers all the areas where I see confusion today. Once A1 is drafted, I can review it from the reception and clinical workflow angle.

Works for me too. For T1, I can focus on the retail-facing parts: front corner, reception display, waiting area stand, and the cupboard behind reception. I will list the product categories per shelf and note where items are hard to reach or see.

I can take the clinical storage for T1: treatment room shelves, trolley, clean utility cupboard, fridge, back room overstock, and the high-level zones for the locked cabinet. I will sketch the current layout and highlight where sterile and non-sterile items are mixed so we can fix that in the new zoning.

Thanks all. To keep things clear: I will own consolidating everything into the A1 layout map once the photos and notes for T1 are ready. Can you share your photos and category lists in our shared folder by tomorrow afternoon so I can draft A1 the next morning?
Yes, I can get the photos and quick notes for my areas into the folder by tomorrow lunchtime so you have them in time to build A1.

Same here, I will upload my retail shelf photos and a simple list of categories per shelf by tomorrow afternoon. I might need a quick check from you later to make sure I grouped some of the supplements correctly.
I will map the clinical areas and share sketches and notes by tomorrow morning so you can start shaping A1. I will also add a short list of current pain points per zone to support T1.

Great, thanks. To close this out: we have agreed the final list of shelves and zones for scope, and I will own updating and maintaining the A1 layout map based on your T1 inputs, aiming for a first draft the day after tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on the new standard shelf layout and zoning

messages.text: I have uploaded the first draft of the new layout map in A1, based on the T1 mapping. It shows proposed zones for retail (front corner, reception display, waiting stand) and for clinical supplies (treatment room, clean utility, fridge, back room, locked cabinet zones). For T2, we now need to agree the standard layout for retail and for medical supplies. Please review the map and comment on: 1) whether the retail flow makes sense for patients, and 2) whether the clinical zones support quick, safe access.

Looking at the retail part of A1: I like that cough and cold items are grouped together and moved to eye level, and that food items are now on a separate lower shelf. One concern: the vitamins and supplements are split between the front corner and the waiting area stand. Would it be better for T2 if we keep all vitamins in one zone so patients do not have to look in two places?

I agree, having vitamins in one place would make it easier to restock and explain to patients. Maybe we can keep the full range in the front corner and use the waiting area stand only for a small seasonal selection, clearly labelled as such in A1.

From the reception side, the new layout in A1 looks better: impulse items are closer to the card machine, and we have removed anything that could confuse patients about what is for sale versus what is for clinical use. For T2, I would just ask that we keep the reception display limited to small, quick-explainer items so we do not block the counter space we need for paperwork.

On the clinical side of A1: I like that sharps and blood collection items are now in a single zone near the treatment chair, and that sterile dressings are separated from non-sterile. One thing I would adjust for T2 is to move high-risk injectable meds to the top shelf of the locked cabinet zone, away from look-alike vials, and keep emergency items grouped together with clear labels.

Good point on vitamins. For the standard retail layout in T2, I propose: all vitamins and supplements in one main zone in the front corner, sorted by type, and the waiting area stand used only for a small seasonal feature that mirrors items already in the main zone. I will update A1 to reflect that and mark the waiting stand as a promo-only zone.

That works for me. With that change, the retail flow feels clear: cough and cold together, vitamins together, food separate, and small items near the till. I do not have any other changes to suggest for the retail layout in A1.
Same here, I am happy with the retail layout as updated in A1. It will make stock checks and price checks easier too.

On the medical supplies: I support moving high-risk injectables to the top shelf and grouping emergency items. We just need to make sure this still matches our clinical protocols and any notes we keep in A8. I can check with the health and safety officer and confirm that the proposed zones in A1 meet their expectations for T7.

Thanks. For T7, I will also double-check temperature-sensitive items in the fridge zone and make sure high-risk items are stored according to protocol. I will add notes into A8 so we have evidence of how the new layout supports clinical requirements.

I have now updated A1 with: 1) vitamins consolidated in the front corner, waiting stand as promo-only; 2) high-risk injectables moved to the top shelf zone; 3) emergency meds grouped and highlighted; 4) clear separation of sterile and non-sterile items. Please take a final look and confirm if this works as our standard layout for both retail and medical supplies under T2 and T7.

I have reviewed the updated A1 and it looks good from both reception and clinical workflow perspectives. I will still get a quick confirmation from the health and safety officer, but I am comfortable treating this as the standard layout for medical supplies for T7, assuming they do not raise any new issues.

I am happy with the clinical zoning in A1 as well. It supports quick access during procedures and keeps high-risk items clearly separated. Once we log the compliance notes in A8 and get the health and safety confirmation, I think we can treat the medical layout as approved.

To close this thread: we have agreed on the standard retail layout in A1, with vitamins consolidated and clear separation of food and medical items, and we have aligned on the medical supply layout pending the formal health and safety confirmation. I will mark the retail layout as approved for T2 and the medical layout as the proposed standard for T7 and A8.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise rotation, expiry, and inspection procedures

messages.text: I have drafted a first version of the stock rotation and expiry-check procedure in A2 and a matching daily and weekly inspection checklist in A4, based on T3 and T5. The proposal is: daily quick check for high-risk and high-turnover items, and weekly deeper check for everything else. Can you review and comment on whether the frequencies and responsibilities per shift feel realistic?

Looking at A2, I see daily checks for fridge items, cough and cold, and dressings, and weekly checks for vitamins and slower movers. For the retail side, daily might be a bit much for vitamins, but weekly is fine. For food items, I would suggest we add them to the daily quick check because of expiry and hygiene.

On A4, the daily checklist looks manageable for the early shift: quick scan of fridge, food items, and high-risk meds, plus a spot check of one retail shelf. The weekly checklist is longer, but if we spread it across shifts it should be ok. Maybe we can assign specific zones to each shift so it is clear who does what for T5.

From a clinical perspective, I would add a daily check for any items used in blood collection and wound care, since those are used frequently and must not be expired. For T3, I also suggest we define a clear rule: always rotate new stock to the back and bring older stock to the front, and document that step in A2 so new staff can follow it easily.

I like the structure in A4. To make it practical for shifts, we could set: early shift does the daily checks for fridge, food, and high-risk meds; late shift does a quick visual check of retail shelves and tidies labels. For the weekly checklist, we can assign one main zone per day so we do not end up with everything on Friday.

Good catch on food items. I will update A2 so that food products are part of the daily quick check, and keep vitamins on the weekly list. I will also add the explicit rotate-back rule that 362964 mentioned, and reflect the shift responsibilities in A4 for T3 and T5.

With those changes, the frequencies look right to me: daily for fridge, food, high-risk meds, and high-use clinical items; weekly for everything else. I can handle the daily checks on my shifts without it slowing down other tasks.
Agreed. The daily and weekly split in A2 and A4 feels balanced now. I like that the checklist spells out which shift does what, that will help new staff pick it up quickly.

I am comfortable with the proposed frequencies as well. For T3, we just need to make sure the health and safety officer reviews A2, especially the parts about high-risk meds and fridge checks, before we call it final.
I can send A2 to the health and safety officer today and ask them to confirm the rotation and expiry-check steps, especially for clinical items. Once they sign off, we can treat T3 as validated.

I have now updated A4 with: 1) daily checks assigned to early shift for fridge, food, high-risk meds, and high-use clinical items; 2) late shift visual check of retail shelves and labels; 3) weekly checklist split by zone across the week. Can you all do a quick read to confirm this version works before we lock it in for T5?
I have read through the updated A4 and it looks clear. The tick boxes per zone per day will make it easy to see what is done. I am ok with this as our final checklist.
Same here, A4 is straightforward to follow. No extra changes from me.
I am happy with A4 as well. Once the health and safety officer confirms A2, we will have a solid pair of documents for rotation and inspection.

Thanks all. We have aligned on the rotation and expiry-check frequencies per category and agreed the final version of the daily and weekly inspection checklist in A4. I will mark T3 and T5 as ready pending the formal health and safety confirmation on A2.

threads.thread_goal: Align labelling, pricing, and training approach before relayout

messages.text: Ahead of the physical relayout, I have drafted the labelling and pricing guideline in A3 for T4 and a quick-reference training guide in A5 for T8 and T9. A3 covers label format, required info, and how we update prices in line with billing rules. A5 is a one-page visual per zone. Please review and flag anything that might confuse staff or cause price mismatches.

In A3, I like that the label format is consistent. One question: for multi-buy offers, do we need a separate line on the label, or is it enough to show the total price for the offer? I want to avoid confusion at the till if the billing system expects a certain format.

On A5, the zone visuals are clear. For the clinical zones, could we add a small reminder about not placing personal items on clinical shelves and keeping labels visible? That often slips during busy times.

For clinical supplies, I suggest we keep labels simple: product name, size, and any key warning, but no prices. That way we avoid confusion between clinical stock and retail items. A3 already hints at this, but maybe we can make it explicit that clinical-only items do not carry prices on the shelf.

On the training side, A5 looks like something we can easily walk through in a short huddle. For T9, I think 15-minute sessions per shift should be enough if we focus on: new zones, rotation basics, and how to handle price changes using A3.

Good question. For multi-buy offers, the billing system expects the unit price plus a clear note of the offer. I will update A3 so labels show: standard unit price, then a second line with the offer (for example: 2 for X). I will also add a reminder to cross-check any new offer with the finance and billing coordinator before printing labels for T4.

Agreed on clinical labels. I will make it explicit in A3 that clinical-only items have non-priced labels with name, size, and key warning only. That should help avoid any confusion with patients about what is for sale.

I will add a small reminder on each clinical zone page in A5 about keeping shelves clear of personal items and not covering labels. That should reinforce the message during training and on the job for T8.

For T9, I suggest we run three types of huddles: 1) retail-focused (front corner, offers, A3), 2) clinical-focused (zones, rotation, A2 and A5), and 3) mixed for reception staff who touch both. Each about 15 minutes, as you suggested, scheduled across early and late shifts.

I like the idea of separate retail and clinical huddles. For the retail one, can we include a quick demo of how to change a label correctly using A3, including where to note the date and initials? That is something people often forget.
Happy to help run the mixed huddles. We can use A5 as the main visual and walk people through one example zone from retail and one from clinical, plus a quick reminder on rotation from A2.

I have now updated A3 with: 1) clear format for multi-buy offers; 2) explicit rule that clinical-only items have non-priced labels; 3) a step to cross-check any new price or offer with the finance and billing coordinator before printing. Please confirm if you are comfortable treating A3 as our guideline for rollout under T4.
I am happy with the updated A3. The steps are clear and should prevent most price mismatches as long as we follow the cross-check with finance.
A3 looks good to me too. The examples at the end will help when we are changing labels on the floor.
Agreed, I am comfortable using A3 as the standard for labelling and pricing during the rollout.

On training dates for T9, I propose: day 1 afternoon for retail huddles, day 2 morning for clinical huddles, and day 2 late afternoon for mixed huddles. That way everyone is trained before we start the physical relayout for T6. Does that work with your shifts?
Those dates work for me. I can support the clinical and mixed huddles, especially to explain how A2 and A4 tie into the new layout.
Works for my rota as well. I can cover the retail huddles on day 1 and help with the mixed one on day 2.
I am on the late shift both days, so I can attend the retail and mixed huddles. Timing looks fine.

Great, then we will go ahead with A3 as the approved labelling and pricing guideline and the training plan as proposed: short huddles over two days using A5 as the main visual. I will also send A3 to the finance and billing coordinator for their formal sign-off on T4.

threads.thread_goal: Monitor rollout, capture issues, and agree on follow-up improvements

messages.text: We are at the start of rollout week. Shelves are being rearranged according to A1 under T6, and we have A4 and A2 live for checks. Please log any stockouts, misplacements, or expiry finds in the A6 issue log for T10, and share quick observations here so we can feed them into the post-rollout review in A7 and T11.

First quick update from the front corner: the new zones from A1 are working, but I noticed two issues. 1) We had a brief stockout on one cough syrup because I moved items before checking the back room. 2) One food item was still mixed in with dressings on the trolley. I have fixed both and logged them in A6 for T10.

From the treatment room: the new layout makes it easier to find dressings, but I found two boxes of sterile gauze with short expiry dates at the back. I rotated them to the front and logged the find in A6. The daily checks from A4 helped catch this early.

Clinically, the new zones are working well. One observation: during a busy period, someone placed used packaging on the clean shelf, covering a couple of labels. I removed it and reminded the team, and I have added a note in A6. Maybe we should reinforce this point in A5 during refreshers.

At reception, the new display is clearer for patients. We had one price query where the shelf label did not match the billing system for a vitamin. I corrected the label using A3 and logged the incident in A6. I will also check with finance to see if there were any recent price updates we missed for T4.

Thanks for logging those. For the stockout, let us add a small reminder in the T6 process: before moving items on the shelf, check back room stock and pull forward anything that matches the new zone. I will note that in our working doc so we can include it in the final A7 review.
Good idea. I will follow that check from now on and add a quick note in A6 if I see any other similar cases.

One more small thing: the weekly checklist in A4 took a bit longer than expected on the first run because I was still learning the new zones. I think it will speed up, but maybe we can review after a week and see if any steps can be simplified.
I agree we should reinforce the clean shelf rule. Maybe in the next short huddle we can use A5 to show a before and after picture and remind everyone not to leave packaging on clinical shelves.
I can add that to the next round of micro-huddles. I will also update A5 with a small visual showing a clear shelf versus one with clutter, so the message sticks.

Let us keep an eye on the time it takes to complete the weekly A4 checklist over this first week. We can use the A6 log and your feedback to see if any steps can be merged or moved to the daily quick checks when we do T11.

Quick note on patient flow: with the new layout, people are spending less time searching the front corner, but a couple of patients still walked over to the waiting stand looking for vitamins. I guided them to the main zone and logged the confusion in A6 so we can decide later if we need extra signage for T12.
Thanks for noting that. For T12, we might add a small sign on the waiting stand pointing to the main vitamin zone. I will test a simple sign this week and see if it reduces the confusion.

On clinical flow, the new zones have reduced time to find dressings and blood collection items. I have not seen any new bottlenecks in the treatment room, but I will keep checking during busy clinics and add notes to A6 if anything comes up for T12.

We are mid-week now, and A6 already has a good set of entries on stockouts, misplacements, expiry finds, and a couple of price issues. I will start grouping them into themes in a draft A7 so we can use that for the T11 review at the end of the week.

For the T11 review, I suggest we focus on three questions: 1) Are there any zones in A1 that still cause confusion? 2) Are the A2 and A4 checks catching issues early enough? 3) Do we need any tweaks to A3 or A5 based on what we see in A6?

I like that structure. From my side, the main theme so far is that the new layout works, but we need to keep reinforcing rotation and label visibility. I will add a couple more notes into A6 after the next weekly check so they are captured for A7.

End of week update: I have drafted A7 with a summary of A6 entries and proposed tweaks: 1) add a pre-move back room check to T6; 2) add a small sign on the waiting stand pointing to the main vitamin zone for T12; 3) reinforce clean shelf rules and label visibility in A5 and future huddles; 4) keep A4 as is but review timing again in a month. Please confirm if you are ok with these adjustments so we can close out the initial rollout review.
Those tweaks make sense to me. The pre-move back room check will help avoid stockouts, and the sign for vitamins should reduce confusion. I am ok with keeping A4 as is for now.
I agree with the proposed adjustments. From the clinical side, the main thing is reinforcing the clean shelf and rotation rules, which you have already captured in A5 and A7.

I am aligned as well. I will take the action to put up the vitamin sign and update A5 with the clean shelf visual. With that, I think we can treat the initial rollout as complete and move into normal monitoring using A4 and A6.

Thanks everyone. We have completed the first rollout week, captured issues in A6, and agreed the follow-up tweaks documented in A7. We will keep using A4 for regular checks and revisit the layout and processes in a month if the logs show new patterns.
